newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-SWISS KERNEN STUNS WITH DOWNHILL GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SWISS KERNEN STUNS WITH DOWNHILL GOLD.

text.p: Bruno Kernen gave Switzerland their first Alpine skiing world championship gold medal in four years on Saturday when he upset the race favourites to win the men's downhill.
Norway's Lasse Kjus was second while Italy's Kristian Ghedina, a pre-race favourite, was third.

The Italian crowd was already celebrating what it had assumed was a victory for local hero Ghedina when 14th starter Kernen headed off down the Kandahar piste and clocked a near-faultless one minute 51.11 seconds.
Kjus caused another upset by starting 18th and clocking 1:51.18 to push Ghedina down the podium.
Before Saturday, Kernen's best result of the season was a third in a World Cup combined event in January and a silver medal in the combined here on Thursday.
Neither Kernen nor Kjus, who has been recovering from illness, have been on a downhill podium this season.
The Swiss, men or women, have not won a world title since Urs Lehmann's surprise downhill win in 1993.
Ghedina could count himself lucky even to get a medal, finishing just 0.01 ahead of Austrian Fritz Strobl.
The Austrian had been more than one second faster than Ghedina at one intermediate timing but lost it when he slipped on a treacherous curve on the lower part of the piste.
The same bend killed off the hopes of Austrian frontrunner Werner Franz, who lost his balance and both skis.
Franz careered heavily into the side-netting and later walked away clutching his left arm and wrist.
Defending 1996 champion Patrick Ortlieb skewed sideways violently higher up but regained his balance. He finished but the error put paid to any chances of a medal.
France's Luc Alphand, downhill World Cup winner for the past two seasons and a favourite after three wins this season, crashed after doing the splits when his skis parted.
